T3. Long-term development [YES] — neutral expert decision due July 2027; broader India-Pakistan water rights trajectory

Synopsis:
The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled that India must uphold the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty — suspended by India in 2025 following a deadly Kashmir attack — and must cap construction on the Ratle Hydroelectric Plant until a World Bank-appointed neutral expert rules by July 2027. India flatly rejected the verdict, denying the court's jurisdiction. The dispute centers on water access critical to Pakistani agriculture and India's infrastructure ambitions in Kashmir. The ruling escalates a legal-diplomatic confrontation between two nuclear-armed states, with India signaling it will proceed regardless.
